summary: opencode-engos-ai postinstall drops opaque platform binary system-wide under unrelated name 'innexarcode'
details: The postinstall script in opencode-engos-ai@1.20.6 resolves the latest (mutable, unpinned) version of a platform/arch-specific sibling package (e.g. opencode-engos-linux-x64) via `npm view <name> version`, installs it into a temporary directory with `npm install --ignore-scripts`, extracts the shipped `bin/opencode` binary, chmods 0755, and unconditionally creates system-wide symlinks at `/usr/local/bin/innexarcode` and `/usr/bin/innexarcode` pointing at the extracted binary. The fetched binary is opaque (payload lives in a separate npm package resolved at install time, not shipped in this tarball) and is fetched without hash or signature verification against a mutable 'latest' tag. The symlink name `innexarcode` matches neither the package name (`opencode-engos-ai`) nor the declared `bin` entry (`opencode-engos`) and is not documented in the tarball, placing an unrelated command on the installer's PATH without disclosure. The package name is also a lookalike of the legitimate `opencode-ai`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
